key_insight: DashAttention replaces hard top-k block selection with a differentiable, adaptive sparse hierarchical attention mechanism so the model learns how many and which tokens to attend to per query while preserving end-to-end gradient flow.
problem_solved: Existing hierarchical attention methods fix the number of selected tokens (top-k) and break gradient flow between coarse (sparse) and fine (dense) stages, limiting adaptivity and learnability of sparse attention patterns.
method: Introduce a differentiable selection mechanism (continuous relaxation / soft gating) to replace non‑differentiable top-k block selection so gradients propagate through sparsification.
Make sparsity adaptive per query by learning selection weights or thresholds, allowing variable number of relevant KV blocks instead of a fixed k.
Retain hierarchical computation: coarse block scoring → adaptive selection → fine-grained softmax attention on selected tokens, yielding efficient compute with end-to-end training.
impact: Enables models to learn task-specific, per-query sparsity for attention, improving compute/accuracy trade-offs and making sparse hierarchical attention trainable end-to-end—useful for large Transformer models and resource-constrained deployment.
visual_elements: Pipeline diagram: coarse block scoring → differentiable/adaptive selector (with gradient arrows) → fine-grained attention on selected tokens
Comparison chart: compute (FLOPs or latency) vs. accuracy for Top-k methods vs. DashAttention
Heatmap visuals: example attention maps showing fixed top-k patterns vs. adaptive per-query sparsity
Icon set: gradient/flow icon to emphasize end-to-end differentiability, clock/bolt for efficiency
paper_title: DashAttention: Differentiable and Adaptive Sparse Hierarchical Attention
paper_authors: Yuxiang Huang, Nuno M. T. Gonçalves, Federico Alvetreti, Lei Li, Xu Han
